deep.reconstruction:
This page has no derivations. It is a prose draft that closes the historical part of Riemann's Habilitationsschrift 'Über die Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe' (written 1854, published posthumously by Dedekind in 1867). It then gives the heading of the main investigation, §7.

Paragraph 1 states where the question stands. Whether a function f can be written as a trigonometric series a0/2 + sum_n (a_n cos nx + b_n sin nx) had so far been settled only under two hypotheses:
(A) f is integrable throughout ('durchgehends Integration zulässt');
(B) f does not have infinitely many maxima and minima.
This is Dirichlet's 1829 setting: piecewise monotone, with finitely many discontinuities.

Riemann then explains why each hypothesis matters:
- If (B) is dropped, Dirichlet's two integral theorems (the limit theorems for sin(kx)/sin x kernels) are insufficient to decide the question.
- If (A) is dropped, the Fourier determination of coefficients, a_n = (1/pi) * integral of f(x) cos(nx) over (-pi, pi) and likewise for b_n, cannot even be applied.

He concludes that the method of the following investigation, which assumes nothing special about f, is forced by this situation. A method as direct as Dirichlet's is impossible by the nature of the problem. In the published text this means the method starts from a given trigonometric series, not from f.

The heading of §7 follows: 'Untersuchung der Darstellbarkeit einer Function durch eine trigonometrische Reihe, ohne besondere Voraussetzungen über die Natur der Function'.

The draft agrees almost word for word with the published §3 ending and §7 heading. The corrections visible on the page bring the wording toward the printed version:
- 'bisher' becomes 'also bis jetzt';
- 'stetig' becomes 'durchgehends';
- 'Sätze' becomes 'Integraltheoreme';
- 'schon' is inserted;
- 'Gang' becomes 'Weg'.

The next page (folio 40v) belongs to the integral section (§5 of the published version). It derives the Riemann integrability criterion: the sum of interval lengths times oscillations, δ1D1 + δ2D2 + ..., must become arbitrarily small. It then shows that bounded functions with finitely many extrema are integrable. The bound used for a monotone function is sum δ_i D_i < d (f(b) - f(a)).
errors: No mathematical errors on this page; it is a historical and methodological statement that matches the published version.

results.what: Assessment that the representability question had been settled only under Dirichlet's conditions (integrability and finitely many extrema), and why each condition is needed (Dirichlet integral theorems vs. Fourier coefficient formula)
results.modern_name: Dirichlet conditions for convergence of Fourier series; motivation for Riemann's theory of general trigonometric series
results.usually_credited_to: Dirichlet (1829) for the theorem; Riemann (Habilitationsschrift 1854, publ. 1867) for this critical assessment

results.what: Programme heading (§7): study representability without special hypotheses on f, necessarily by an indirect route starting from the series
results.modern_name: Riemann's theory of trigonometric series (formal double integration F(x), Riemann's first and second lemmas)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of a passage in Riemann's published Habilitationsschrift, nearly verbatim. It contains nothing new beyond minor wording variants.
